proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\mathcal Q\) for the set of quadruples
\[
 Q=(k,R_1,R_2,W),
 \qquad k\in[K],\qquad
 R_1,R_2,W\subseteq U_k
\]
such that the three vertex sets are pairwise disjoint and \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are \(m\)-connected given \(W\) in the replacement MAG. The set \(\mathcal Q\) is finite because \(K\), every domain \(U_k\), and every variable alphabet are finite.

Fix \(Q=(k,R_1,R_2,W)\) and a cell assignment \(a=(r_1,r_2,w)\). Define
\[
 \Delta_{Q,a}(\theta)
 :=p_{\theta,k}(r_1,r_2,w)p_{\theta,k}(w)
   -p_{\theta,k}(r_1,w)p_{\theta,k}(r_2,w).
 \tag{1}
\]
Strict positivity of every full cell implies \(p_{\theta,k}(w)>0\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\) and every \(w\); when \(W=\varnothing\), this marginal is \(1\). Therefore the definition of conditional independence for a finite table gives
\[
 X_{R_1}\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{R_2}\mid X_W
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{p_{\theta,k}(r_1,r_2,w)}{p_{\theta,k}(w)}
 =
 \frac{p_{\theta,k}(r_1,w)}{p_{\theta,k}(w)}
 \frac{p_{\theta,k}(r_2,w)}{p_{\theta,k}(w)}
 \quad\text{for every }a,
 \tag{2}
\]
and multiplication by the positive number \(p_{\theta,k}(w)^2\) shows that (2) is equivalent to
\[
 \Delta_{Q,a}(\theta)=0
 \quad\text{for every cell assignment }a.
 \tag{3}
\]
All masses and hence all marginals in (1) are rational functions of \(\theta\). By the stipulated denominator positivity, clearing a common denominator produces a polynomial \(q_{Q,a}\) and a function \(d_{Q,a}(\theta)>0\) on \(\Theta\) such that
\[
 q_{Q,a}(\theta)=d_{Q,a}(\theta)\Delta_{Q,a}(\theta).
 \tag{4}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 q_{Q,a}(\theta)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Delta_{Q,a}(\theta)=0
 \qquad(\theta\in\Theta).
 \tag{5}
\]

Suppose first that for every \(Q\in\mathcal Q\) at least one \(q_{Q,a}\) is not the zero polynomial. Choose one such assignment \(a(Q)\) for each \(Q\), and set
\[
 Q_*(\theta):=\prod_{Q\in\mathcal Q}q_{Q,a(Q)}(\theta),
 \tag{6}
\]
with the empty product equal to \(1\). Since a polynomial ring over \(\mathbb R\) is an integral domain, finiteness of \(\mathcal Q\) and the choice of the factors imply that \(Q_*\) is not the zero polynomial.

We record the elementary fact needed to locate a common parameter. A nonzero real polynomial in \(r\) variables cannot vanish on a nonempty open subset of \(\mathbb R^r\). For \(r=0\) the assertion concerns a nonzero constant. For \(r=1\) it follows by repeated division by \(t-t_0\), which bounds the number of distinct roots by the degree. Inductively, write a polynomial in \(r\) variables as
\[
 h(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}h_j(t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1})t_r^j.
 \tag{7}
\]
If \(h\) vanished on an open box, then for every point in the box's projection the resulting univariate polynomial would vanish on an interval, so every coefficient \(h_j\) would vanish on the projected open box. The induction hypothesis would make every \(h_j\) the zero polynomial, contrary to \(h\ne0\). Since every nonempty open set contains an open box, the fact follows.

Apply this fact to \(Q_*\) and the nonempty open set \(\Theta\). There is \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) such that
\[
 Q_*(\theta^\star)\ne0.
 \tag{8}
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q\), equations (6) and (8) give \(q_{Q,a(Q)}(\theta^\star)\ne0\). Equations (3)--(5) then imply
\[
 X_{R_1}\not\!\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{R_2}\mid X_W
 \quad\text{under }P_{\eta_{\theta^\star},k}^{\mathrm{pool}}
 \qquad\text{for every }Q\in\mathcal Q.
 \tag{9}
\]
For a query that is \(m\)-separated in its replacement MAG, the assumed Markov direction gives the corresponding conditional independence. Combining this implication with (9) yields, for every \(k\in[K]\) and every disjoint \(R_1,R_2,W\subseteq U_k\),
\[
 X_{R_1}\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{R_2}\mid X_W
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 R_1\text{ and }R_2\text{ are }m\text{-separated by }W.
 \tag{10}
\]
Thus all pooled laws are simultaneously faithful. The parameter-family premise already supplies one coupled product-exogenous shared-response model satisfying every other member condition of \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\), including non-target response sharing, the common basal selection response, and positive basal selection probability. Equation (10) supplies the only possibly missing condition, pooled twin faithfulness. Hence \(\eta_{\theta^\star}\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\). Its selection-set, basal-graph, and target components equal \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) by hypothesis, so \(\mathrm{def:replacement\mbox{-}realization\mbox{-}fiber}\) gives
\[
 \eta_{\theta^\star}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B).
 \tag{11}
\]
The role of \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\) is to guarantee that the common graphical specification used here has the declared acyclic selected-DAG structure and the required replacement MAG signatures; no coupling is inferred from that graphical lemma.

Conversely, suppose \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) makes every pooled selected law faithful to its replacement MAG. For any \(Q\in\mathcal Q\), faithfulness and \(m\)-connection imply failure of the corresponding conditional independence. By (3), there is a cell assignment \(a\) with \(\Delta_{Q,a}(\theta^\star)\ne0\). Equations (4)--(5) give
\[
 q_{Q,a}(\theta^\star)\ne0,
 \tag{12}
\]
so \(q_{Q,a}\) is not the zero polynomial. This proves atomic nontriviality for every \(m\)-connected query and establishes the converse. If \(K=0\), both the collection of pooled faithfulness requirements and \(\mathcal Q\) are empty; the equivalence is vacuous, any point of the nonempty \(\Theta\) is admissible, and (11) follows from the directly parameterized member conditions. This completes the proof.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and a graph \(B\) admissible for the graphical replacement lemma. Suppose that a nonempty open set \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^r\) directly parameterizes finite-alphabet ambient tuples \(\eta_\theta\) whose selection-set, basal-graph, and target components jointly equal \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\). Assume that every \(\eta_\theta\) satisfies every member condition in \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) except possibly pooled twin faithfulness. In particular, each tuple is already represented by one product law of mutually independent exogenous variables whose same realized vector is used in every world, measurable response functions shared across regimes at every non-target vertex, one basal selection response generated before intervention, and positive basal selection probability; these coupled-response objects are part of the parameterized tuple and are not reconstructed from regime-local conditional tables. For \(k\in[K]\), let \(p_{\theta,k}\) be the mass function of the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta_\theta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), and let the replacement MAG be the latent projection on \(U_k\) determined by \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\). Assume that every cell of \(p_{\theta,k}\) is strictly positive and rational in \(\theta\), with all denominators positive on \(\Theta\), and that \(m\)-separation in every replacement MAG implies the corresponding conditional independence under \(p_{\theta,k}\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\). For every \(k\in[K]\), every triple of pairwise disjoint sets \(R_1,R_2,W\subseteq U_k\), and every cell assignment \(a=(r_1,r_2,w)\), clear positive denominators in
\[
 p_{\theta,k}(r_1,r_2,w)p_{\theta,k}(w)
 -p_{\theta,k}(r_1,w)p_{\theta,k}(r_2,w)
\]
and denote the resulting polynomial by \(q_{k,R_1,R_2,W,a}\). There exists \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) for which all pooled selected laws are simultaneously faithful to their replacement MAGs if and only if, for every query \((k,R_1,R_2,W)\) that is \(m\)-connected in its replacement MAG, at least one polynomial \(q_{k,R_1,R_2,W,a}\) is not the zero polynomial. Every such simultaneously faithful \(\eta_{\theta^\star}\) belongs to \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). Thus the conclusion is conditional on the supplied directly coupled rational parameterization and reduces faithful realization within that family to atomic determinant nontriviality; it constructs neither the parameterization nor the atomic certificates.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The prior premise of regime-local factorization and equal non-target conditional tables does not itself supply the one-product-law, same-realized-noise, shared-response cross-world coupling required by the model class. The corrected claim narrows the premise to a directly parameterized coupled-response tuple family and uses the determinant argument only to add pooled twin faithfulness.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For every admissible replacement specification, construct a nonempty open rational parameterization of directly coupled shared-exogenous, shared-response twin-SCM tuples satisfying every model-class condition except possibly pooled twin faithfulness; then, for each query that is \(m\)-connected in a replacement MAG, exhibit a cell determinant that is not the zero polynomial on that parameter space.
open_obligations.obstruction: Generic faithfulness for unrestricted multinomial DAGs does not establish nontriviality after one common basal selection response, fixed one-half pooling, non-target response equalities, and same-realized-exogenous cross-world coupling are imposed. The graphical replacement lemma controls projection signatures but supplies neither a coupled probability parameter space nor an atomic dependence witness.
open_obligations.attempted: The finite exceptional-set argument was completed on any supplied directly coupled rational parameter family: all unfaithfulness events become determinant zero sets and a product-polynomial argument selects one simultaneous faithful point once atomic nontriviality holds. This argument cannot prove that the constrained family exists for every replacement or that a required determinant does not vanish identically.
open_obligations.partial_result: For any supplied nonempty open set \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^r\) that directly parameterizes finite-alphabet tuples already carrying one product exogenous law, the same realized exogenous vector in every world, response functions shared off target, one basal pre-intervention selection response, positive basal selection probability, and every other model-class condition except possibly pooled twin faithfulness, the remaining genericity step is finite and algebraic. If the pooled selected cell masses are strictly positive rational functions with positive denominators and the Markov direction holds, conditional independence is equivalent to the vanishing of finitely many cleared determinant polynomials. Choosing one nonzero polynomial for each \(m\)-connected query and taking their product yields a point \(\theta^\star\) at which all pooled laws are simultaneously faithful. Conversely, simultaneous faithfulness implies that at least one determinant polynomial for each \(m\)-connected query is nonzero. What remains unproved is the construction of such a directly coupled nonempty open rational parameter family for every admissible replacement and the atomic nontriviality certificate for every \(m\)-connected query on that constrained family.

prose_updates.tldr: Selection before perturbation couples every pooled regime through one basal selected DAG and one shared-response twin SCM. The proved structural result is the exact fixed-\(A\) graphical identity \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\). At law level, the faithful mark set is nonempty and contained in that graphical set, so singleton graphical sets give equality automatically; two-mark faithful witnesses require nonempty realization fibers. On any supplied directly coupled nonempty open rational parameter family, atomic nonzero determinant certificates imply simultaneous pooled faithfulness by a finite exceptional-set argument. Constructing that parameter family, proving the atomic certificates, finding a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension, establishing canonical endpoint equality, and obtaining simultaneous separation-margin confidence SI-PAGs remain open. The achieved result is therefore below a complete-calculus result. Neither faithful realization nor the unknown-\(A\) extension follows from graphical inclusion.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al.'s graphical endpoint semantics do not furnish two faithful representatives from one basal selected DAG and one coupled shared-response twin SCM. The law-level gap has two parts: for every admissible replacement, construct a directly coupled nonempty open rational parameter family satisfying all model conditions except possibly pooled twin faithfulness, and prove a nonzero cleared determinant for every \(m\)-connected query on that family. Separately, no finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension theorem synchronizes the common exterior completion across regimes. The parameter construction, atomic certificates, finite rule list, canonical equality, and separation-margin confidence result all remain open.
project_justification.niche: The note delivers the exact fixed-\(A\) structural characterization \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\), then cleanly separates it from the nonempty faithful inclusion and from the open unknown-\(A\) problem. Singleton graphical mark sets identify the faithful endpoint, whereas a two-mark graphical set reaches law-level equality only when both required realization fibers are nonempty. This is a technical foundation below a complete-calculus result.
project_justification.fill: Explicit empty-graph and signature-monotone-path replacements establish the two graphical marks while preserving the full regime signatures. The faithful-model mark set is nonempty and lies inside the exact graphical set, giving automatic equality in singleton cases and only a conditional equality in the two-mark case. For a supplied directly coupled rational parameterization, the determinant proof shows that atomic nontriviality is sufficient and necessary for a common simultaneously faithful parameter. If faithful realization and a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension are later established, the existing conditional theorem yields canonical endpoint equality and at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. Neither antecedent is a consequence of graphical inclusion, and no simultaneous confidence SI-PAG theorem is proved.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The replacement construction specifies a selection set, basal DAG, and intervention targets, but no law-level coupling. The exceptional-set lemma now starts only after a nonempty open rational family of tuples is supplied directly, with one product exogenous law, the same realized vector across worlds, response functions shared off target, one basal selection response, positive selection probability, positive pooled cells, positive rational denominators, and the Markov direction. It adds pooled twin faithfulness when the atomic determinants are nontrivial; it does not construct that family or certify those determinants. The exact graphical identity does not imply two-mark faithful realization, and neither faithful realization nor graphical inclusion supplies a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension. No separation margin or finite-sample testing theorem is supplied, so canonical equality and simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved structural content is the exact fixed-selection-ancestry identity \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\) on the purely graphical Dai fiber. At law level, \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{faith}}\subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}\); singleton \(\mathcal G_A\) gives equality, while two-mark equality requires nonempty faithful realization fibers. The algebraic lemma is conditional on a supplied directly coupled nonempty open rational parameter family satisfying positivity and the Markov direction, plus one nonzero determinant certificate per \(m\)-connected query. Constructing the family, proving those certificates, producing opposing faithful two-mark witnesses, finding a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension rule list, proving unconditional canonical equality, and deriving simultaneous finite-sample confidence guarantees are open. Neither the faithful-realization antecedent nor the unknown-\(A\) extension antecedent follows from graphical inclusion. Thus the result is below a complete-calculus result; a global basal-DAG enumerator is not offered as the headline method.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma proves the finite algebraic exceptional-set step for a supplied directly coupled rational shared-response family; the coupling is a premise, not something reconstructed from regime-local tables.
statement_notes.gap: It constructs neither the directly coupled nonempty open parameter family nor a nonzero determinant certificate for any \(m\)-connected query.
statement_notes.consumer: The faithful-realization question uses the lemma to isolate its two remaining tasks: parameter-family construction and atomic determinant nontriviality.

statement_notes.justification: This open question separates law-level faithful promotion from the exact fixed-\(A\) graphical identity.
statement_notes.gap: For arbitrary admissible replacements, both a directly coupled nonempty open rational parameterization and one nonzero determinant certificate per \(m\)-connected query remain unproved.
statement_notes.consumer: An affirmative answer would promote the two graphical endpoint constructions to faithful law-level witnesses, but would not itself provide the finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension needed for canonical equality.

proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(\mathcal O\) is compatible, \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\neq\varnothing\).  Fix an arbitrary reported endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:monotone\mbox{-}closure}\), the mark assigned by \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) at \(e\) is either a member of \(\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\) or \(\mathtt{circle}\).  We treat these two exhaustive cases.

Suppose first that
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e)=m,
 \qquad m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The soundness condition in the theorem gives
\[
 \mu_\xi(e)=m
 \qquad\text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O).
 \tag{2}
\]
By the invariant-mark clause of \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}si\mbox{-}pag}\), equation \((2)\) implies
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m
 =\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e).
 \tag{3}
\]

Suppose instead that
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Apply the opposing-extension condition first with \(m=\mathtt{tail}\) and then with \(m=\mathtt{arrow}\).  For each \(m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\), it supplies a base model \(\xi_{e,m}\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and a graph \(B_{e,m}\) admissible for \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\) such that
\[
 \mu_{\widetilde\xi}(e)=m
 \quad\text{for every }
 \widetilde\xi\in\operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,m},B_{e,m}).
 \tag{5}
\]
The faithful-realization condition gives
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,m},B_{e,m})\neq\varnothing
 \qquad\text{for each }m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Choose
\[
 \widetilde\xi_m\in
 \operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,m},B_{e,m})
 \qquad\text{for each }m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Since each \(B_{e,m}\) is admissible, \(\mathrm{lem:replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), whose graphical premise is supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), yields
\[
 \mathcal O(\widetilde\xi_m)=\mathcal O,
 \qquad
 \widetilde\xi_m\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\xi_{e,m})
 \subseteq\mathcal C(\mathcal O).
 \tag{8}
\]
Combining \((5)\)--\((8)\) gives two members of the same compatibility fiber with opposing marks:
\[
 \mu_{\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{tail}}}(e)=\mathtt{tail},
 \qquad
 \mu_{\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{arrow}}}(e)=\mathtt{arrow}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the endpoint mark is not invariant over \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\).  The circle clause of \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}si\mbox{-}pag}\) therefore gives
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}
 =\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e).
 \tag{10}
\]

Equations \((3)\) and \((10)\) establish equality at every \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\).  Both objects are partial mixed-graph families on the reported domain fixed by \(\mathcal O\), by \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}si\mbox{-}pag}\) and \(\mathrm{def:monotone\mbox{-}closure}\).  Hence endpointwise equality implies
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O).
 \tag{11}
\]

Finally, suppose that every rule premise and path predicate has the stated uniform polynomial-time decision procedure.  The list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is finite and its schemata are independent of \(D\) and \(K\) by hypothesis.  Membership in \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), together with \(\mathrm{def:monotone\mbox{-}closure}\), ensures that each strict conclusion replaces at least one reported circle by a definite endpoint and that no definite endpoint is subsequently changed.  Therefore all hypotheses of \(\mathrm{prop:exact\mbox{-}conditional\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}saturation}\) hold.  That proposition yields polynomial-time saturation and at most
\[
 (K+1)D(D-1)
\]
strict reported-endpoint updates.  The argument uses the faithful-realization and opposing-extension conditions only as explicit antecedents; it neither establishes them nor constructs the candidate rule list.  This proves the conditional claim.

Put \(g=\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\).  Because \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), the definition of the fixed-\(A\) fiber gives \(\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).  Hence
\[
 \mu_\eta(e)\in\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta),
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)\ne\varnothing.
 \tag{1}
\]
The hypotheses that \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), \(uv\notin H\), and \(uv\) occurs in the regime-\(k\) skeleton are precisely the intervention-created-adjacency hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:exact\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}a\mbox{-}graphical\mbox{-}frontier}\).  That lemma, together with \(g=\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\), yields
\[
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq
 \mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 =\mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
 \tag{2}
\]
Combining (1) and (2) proves the asserted nonempty outer bracket.

Suppose first that \(u\notin Z_k\).  By the three-case definition in \(\mathrm{def:fixed\mbox{-}a\mbox{-}mark\mbox{-}sets}\),
\[
 \mathcal G_A(u,v;k)=\{\mathtt{tail}\}.
\]
A nonempty subset of a singleton is that singleton, so (1)--(2) imply
\[
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{tail}\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Suppose instead that \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=0\).  The same definition gives
\[
 \mathcal G_A(u,v;k)=\{\mathtt{arrow}\},
\]
and therefore (1)--(2) give
\[
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{arrow}\}.
 \tag{4}
\]

It remains to establish the conditional conclusion in the reachability case.  Assume
\[
 u\in Z_k,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1.
 \tag{5}
\]
By the definition of nonempty reachability in \(L_{A(\eta)}\), there is a directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path.  Since \(A(\eta)\subseteq V\) and \(V\) is finite, deleting repeated directed cycles produces a simple directed path \(P\).  Let \(B_0\) be the empty directed graph on \(A(\eta)\), and let \(B_P\) contain exactly the directed edges of \(P\).  The reachability part of \(\mathrm{lem:exact\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}a\mbox{-}graphical\mbox{-}frontier}\) states that both \(B_0\) and \(B_P\) are admissible and that
\[
 \operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_0),\ 
 \operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_P)
 \in\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g).
 \tag{6}
\]
Thus both replacement specifications have ancestral selected set \(A(\eta)\) and preserve the skeleton and the unshielded-collider set of every regime projection on its full domain \(U_j\), including all instances involving \(\zeta_j\).  The same lemma computes their marks at \(e\) as
\[
 \mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_0)}(e)
   =\mathtt{arrow},
 \qquad
 \mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_P)}(e)
   =\mathtt{tail}.
 \tag{7}
\]
This proves the two asserted common-basal graphical witness statements without promoting either specification to a law-level model.

Now impose the two antecedents in the theorem's displayed implication:
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0)\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P)\ne\varnothing.
 \tag{8}
\]
Choose
\[
 \eta_{\mathtt{arrow}}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0),
 \qquad
 \eta_{\mathtt{tail}}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P).
 \tag{9}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), each model in (9) is a fully specified faithful member of \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).  Its graphical reduct is the corresponding replacement specification, so (7) and the definition of \(\mathcal M_A\) imply
\[
 \{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}
 \subseteq\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta).
 \tag{10}
\]
Under (5), the third case of \(\mathrm{def:fixed\mbox{-}a\mbox{-}mark\mbox{-}sets}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal G_A(u,v;k)=\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (2), (10), and (11) therefore establish
\[
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 =\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)
 =\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
\]

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\) gives
\[
 Z_k=T_k(\eta)\cup
 \bigl((F_k(\eta)\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A(\eta)\bigr),
\]
so the proof uses \(u\in Z_k\), which allows either direct targeting or indirect affectedness in \(A(\eta)\), and never replaces this condition by \(u\in T_k(\eta)\).  Moreover, \(\mathrm{prop:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}reduction}\) exhibits a retained adjacency with an arrowhead endpoint outside \(Z_k\).  Consequently the restriction \(uv\notin H\) is necessary for the stated intervention-created-edge bracket.  This completes the proof.
